scope: Independent bounded review of six libxml2 findings only; primary GNOME patches read live and local source/evidence inspected. No runtime changes, exploit attempt, library replacement, or heavy tests.
bindings: System libxml2 2.9.14+dfsg-1.3~deb12u6 remains installed; active LO/lxml libxml2 2.14.6 is not assumed patched for these six.

rows.upstream: dict.c guards QName allocation arithmetic and exponential pool growth.
rows.inference: Accepted XLSX expanded total is30MiB, no DTD expansion, and XML names in generated DOCX come from checksum-pinned templates. These bounds exclude attacker-supplied QName lengths near the unsigned32-bit multiplication overflow; small input cannot grow via DTD entities because preparse rejects their declaration.
rows.claimType: Engineering reachability inference; native vulnerability remains in package

rows.upstream: uri.c rejects xmlStrlen overflow before allocation in URI escaping; relevant input exceeds INT_MAX.
rows.inference: 30MiB expanded XLSX and bounded scalar document inputs cannot supply a multi-gigabyte URI. Form strings become text, while generated relationship resources remain fixed/local. Nonroot isolation alone would not justify exclusion; explicit length/dataflow does.
rows.claimType: Engineering reachability inference; native vulnerability remains in package

rows.upstream: valid.c adds missing buffer-space checks around validation diagnostic string construction.
rows.inference: Untrusted workbook DTDs are rejected before openpyxl parsing. Renderer does not request DTD validation of user input; only checksum-pinned templates supply DOCX XML. Absence of affected DTD diagnostic dataflow supports non-reachability for current inputs.
rows.claimType: Engineering reachability inference; native vulnerability remains in package

rows.upstream: xpointer.c detects xmlStrlen overflow in XPointer evaluation before allocation.
rows.inference: No product XPointer evaluation path found; renderer XPath queries are fixed internal selectors. Generated template XML is pinned and form data is scalar text. No arbitrary XML/DOCX upload is supported. XPointer inclusion would invalidate this conclusion.
rows.claimType: Engineering reachability inference; native vulnerability remains in package

rows.upstream: xmlIO.c checks pending write/flush buffer sizes against INT_MAX before passing the length to a callback.
rows.inference: Worksheet writer streams individual bounded cells/rows via xmlfile; existing exact-binding probe measured76066361 totalXMLbytes over18478callbacks, maximum4316bytes. This supports code review of bounded writes; total file size alone would not prove it. DOCX jobs use bounded recipients/template parts and separate binary image ZIP parts.
rows.claimType: Engineering reachability inference; native vulnerability remains in package

rows.upstream: xinclude.c propagates parser flags into XInclude processing and includes a network-denial regression.
rows.inference: No XInclude processing is called by product source. Template resources are checksum-pinned; user values are text, not inclusion programs. DTD guard and keep_links=false help upstream inputs but are not claimed sufficient to repair XInclude itself. An XInclude/arbitrary DOCX feature would require new review.
rows.claimType: Engineering reachability inference; native vulnerability remains in package

sourceChecks.lines: 343–348 checksum-pinned template;490–497 import size/archive bounds then validate_xlsx_xml before load_workbook; registry cells emitted as text
All XML/rels members streamed through Expat; StartDoctype/Entity/ExternalEntity failclosed, nesting128/attributes128

limitations: No claim of patched native library, zero raw CVEs, or exploit-proof safety for arbitrary XML applications.
No dynamic call graph of every LibreOffice internals path performed. Pinned template/data-only input restriction is part of the conclusion, not ELF import absence alone.
Export callback probe is an existing bounded measurement on exact lxml/libxml binding; reviewer did not rerun it.
Re-review on image/library change, arbitrary DOCX/XML/XInclude/XPointer/DTD feature, input-limit change, or callback/writer change.
This six-CVE review does not independently close all A47 runtime/security findings.
